title: Risk Orchestration — Stoplight Matrix, Phased Rollback Sequences, and Stakeholder Alert Templates
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Purpose: Create a single coordinated artifact and operational workflow to manage release blockers, trigger phased rollback sequences, and send pre-formatted incident communications to internal and external stakeholders. This ticket delivers: (1) a Stoplight Risk Matrix that maps blocker classes to go/no-go gates, (2) phased rollback runbooks with exact operator commands and fallbacks, (3) email/slack/console incident templates for stakeholders (dev, oncall, sales, enterprise customers), and (4) a short cadence for cross-team launch decision checkpoints.

Background: Multiple launches in the last year had ad-hoc rollback decisions and inconsistent comms. That resulted in customer confusion and prolonged mitigation. This artifact will be integrated into the Launch Readiness checklist and referenced in pre-launch checkpoints.

Scope (in-scope):
- Define blocker taxonomy (deploy, performance, correctness, security, infra capacity) and severity tiers.
- Create Stoplight matrix mapping blockers to required mitigations and gate owners.
- Author phased rollback sequences (canary rollback -> capacity surge -> full rollback) with executable steps and runbook links.
- Draft incident communication templates (internal ops, engineering, PM, CS, and external postmortem starter).
- Define decision checkpoints (T-72h, T-6h, T-0) and required signals.

Out of scope:
- Automating rollback via orchestration (ENG follow-up ticket required).
- Full legal/customer notification playbook for regulated customers (will coordinate with Security/Legal separately).
acceptance_criteria: Stoplight Risk Matrix published in Confluence and linked from Launch checklist
Phased rollback runbook has clear operator steps and a tested dry-run with oncall in staging
Three incident templates (internal, enterprise customer, public status) reviewed and signed off by CS and Legal
Cross-team decision checklist created with named gate owners and a rehearsal scheduled before T-0
